title: Symphony No. 5 in B-flat major
hook: A sunny symphony by a nineteen-year-old in love with Mozart, written for friends to play at home.

painting.title: The Hülsenbeck Children
painting.pairingNote: Three children racing through a sunlit garden: the youthful, open-air brightness of a nineteen-year-old’s symphony.

facts: Schubert wrote the symphony in September 1816 and dated the score as finished on 3 October 1816. He was nineteen. It was meant for an amateur orchestra in Vienna founded by Otto Hatwig, in which Schubert played the viola and his brother Ferdinand the violin, and that orchestra gave its first performance that autumn.

That June he wrote in his diary: “O Mozart! immortal Mozart!” The symphony uses the smallest orchestra of all his symphonies: one flute, two oboes, two bassoons, two horns and strings, with no clarinets, trumpets or timpani. Many have compared its light, clear scoring to Mozart’s.
It was not played in public until 17 October 1841, thirteen years after Schubert’s death, and not printed until the 1880s, in the first complete edition of his works, edited by Brahms.
It does not sound like an imitation. Schubert slides into distant keys, turns from major to minor in a moment, and starts the return of the first movement in the “wrong” key.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a bright, quick opening (I), a song without words (II), a stormy minuet with a country-dance trio (III), a light-footed dance to finish (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro
movements.summary: No slow introduction: four bars of woodwind chords and a quick run in the violins, and the main tune is already there. The movement is a [[sonata-form|sonata form]] full of sunlight, with a gentle second theme and a short, wandering development.

mainIdeas.name: The curtain
mainIdeas.description: four bars of soft woodwind chords, with a rising run in the first violins.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a cheerful, rising tune in a dotted rhythm, soft, in the violins, echoed by the basses.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a graceful, singing tune in F major, first in the strings, then in the woodwind.

notice: Listen to the curtain-raising woodwind chords at the start. They return to open the development and, shortened, to lead into the recapitulation.
At ≈ 3:17, notice that the tune comes back, but somehow higher and lighter. Schubert brings it back in a different key from the one it started in.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Beecham recorded the symphony with his Royal Philharmonic Orchestra in sessions between May 1958 and May 1959, partly in the Salle Wagram in Paris and partly at Abbey Road in London. He does not repeat the exposition, which makes his first movement almost a minute and a half shorter than performances that do. On the Spotify album the symphony is tracks 5–8, between Nos. 3 and 6.

movements.heading: Andante con moto
movements.summary: A slow, tender song for orchestra in E-flat major. Its main tune keeps returning, and between its returns the music twice slides into distant, shadowy keys before finding its way home.

mainIdeas.name: The episodes
mainIdeas.description: a darker, yearning tune that drifts into unexpected keys.

movements.heading: Menuetto. Allegro molto – Trio
movements.summary: A brisk, stormy [[minuet|minuet]] in G minor, closer to a country stamping-dance than a court minuet, with a gentle [[trio|trio]] in G major that sounds like a rustic [[landler|Ländler]].

mainIdeas.name: The minuet
mainIdeas.description: a forceful tune in the minor for the whole orchestra, with sharp accents.

mainIdeas.name: The trio
mainIdeas.description: a quiet, folk-like tune in the strings and a solo bassoon, over long-held notes in the bass.

movements.heading: Allegro vivace
movements.summary: A quick, playful finale in [[sonata-form|sonata form]] that seems to dance on its toes. A sudden loud outburst in the minor gives it drama; then the gentle second theme and a busy development keep the mood light. It ends without a big final gesture.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a skipping, dance-like tune in the strings, answered by the woodwind.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a smooth, graceful tune in F major, introduced after a pause.

notice: Listen for how the symphony ends: there is no big final build-up. The music simply finishes its tune and stops.

threads.title: A small orchestra
threads.body: One flute, pairs of oboes, bassoons and horns, and strings. With no trumpets or drums, every instrument can be heard, and the loud moments stay light.

threads.title: Mozart and beyond
threads.body: The clarity and balance recall Mozart, whom Schubert adored that year, but the sudden slides into distant keys are Schubert’s own.

threads.title: Music among friends
threads.body: It was written for an orchestra of amateurs and family, in which the composer himself played viola.
